# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

export async function remind(page: Page, claimId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const c = claimRow(page, claimId);
  const today = await shown(page.getByTestId('sheet-today'));
  const done = async () => (await shown(c.getByTestId('claim-reminded'))) === today;
  const already = await done();
  await c.getByTestId('claim-remind').click();
  return until(page, done, c.getByTestId('claim-error'), 'remind', already);
}

/** Add a comment to a claim: true once the claim shows one more comment line. */
export async function addComment(page: Page, claimId: string, text: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const c = claimRow(page, claimId);
  const lines = c.getByTestId('claim-comments-line');
  const was = await lines.count();
  await c.getByTestId('claim-comment-text').fill(text);
  await c.getByTestId('claim-comment-add').click();
  return until(page, async () => (await lines.count()) > was, c.getByTestId('claim-error'), 'comment');
}

/** Add a holiday to the sheet: true once its row shows. */
export async function addHoliday(page: Page, date: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = page.getByTestId(`holiday-row-${date}`);
  const already = (await r.count()) > 0;
  await page.getByTestId('holiday-date').fill(date);
  await page.getByTestId('holiday-add').click();
  return until(page, async () => (await r.count()) > 0, page.getByTestId('holiday-error'), 'add holiday', already);
}

/** Add a void reason to the sheet's list: true once its row shows. */
export async function addVoidReason(page: Page, reason: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = page.getByTestId(`void-reason-row-${reason.trim()}`);
  const already = reason.trim() !== '' && (await r.count()) > 0;
  await page.getByTestId('void-reason-text').fill(reason);
  await page.getByTestId('void-reason-add').click();
  return until(page, async () => reason.trim() !== '' && (await r.count()) > 0,
    page.getByTestId('void-reason-error'), 'add void reason', already);

export async function remind(page: Page, claimId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const c = claimRow(page, claimId);
  const today = await shown(page.getByTestId('sheet-today'));
  const done = async () => (await shown(c.getByTestId('claim-reminded'))) === today;
  const already = await done();
  await c.getByTestId('claim-remind').click();
  return until(page, done, c.getByTestId('claim-error'), 'remind', already);
}

/** Add a comment to a claim: true once the claim shows one more comment line. */
export async function addComment(page: Page, claimId: string, text: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const c = claimRow(page, claimId);
  const lines = c.getByTestId('claim-comments-line');
  const was = await lines.count();
  await c.getByTestId('claim-comment-text').fill(text);
  await c.getByTestId('claim-comment-add').click();
  return until(page, async () => (await lines.count()) > was, c.getByTestId('claim-error'), 'comment');
}

/** Add a holiday to the sheet: true once its row shows. */
export async function addHoliday(page: Page, date: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = page.getByTestId(`holiday-row-${date}`);
  const already = (await r.count()) > 0;
  await page.getByTestId('holiday-date').fill(date);
  await page.getByTestId('holiday-add').click();
  return until(page, async () => (await r.count()) > 0, page.getByTestId('holiday-error'), 'add holiday', already);
}

/** Add a void reason to the sheet's list: true once its row shows. */
export async function addVoidReason(page: Page, reason: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const r = page.getByTestId(`void-reason-row-${reason.trim()}`);
  const already = reason.trim() !== '' && (await r.count()) > 0;
  await page.getByTestId('void-reason-text').fill(reason);
  await page.getByTestId('void-reason-add').click();
  return until(page, async () => reason.trim() !== '' && (await r.count()) > 0,
    page.getByTestId('void-reason-error'), 'add void reason', already);

The sheet now has a holiday list, and a claim's due-by moves past any holidays when it falls on one. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it behaves**
- A date entry and an add button (`holiday-date`, `holiday-add`) add a date to the list. Each holiday shows as a row (`holiday-row-<date>`).
- Adding a date that's already on the list, or text that isn't a date, is refused: `holiday-error` shows beside the entry and nothing is written. The error clears as soon as the entry is edited or submitted again.
- A successful add writes `HOLIDAY_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> date=<date>` to the audit file.
- As with other changes, a viewer or an archived sheet can't add holidays.
- When a claim is created and its date plus terms lands on a holiday, the due-by becomes the next day that isn't a holiday. It uses the holidays on the sheet at that moment and is stored with the claim, so adding a holiday later leaves existing due-by dates alone.

**Where the change is**
- **Stored data:** a new `holiday` table in `V44__holiday.sql`, with a rule that a sheet can't hold the same date twice.
- **Server:** a new `holiday` package with the code that validates, saves and audits a holiday, plus GET/POST `/api/sheets/{sheetId}/holidays` (`holidays.GET.yml`, `holidays.POST.yml`).
- **Front end:** a new `Holidays.tsx` panel in the settings area, placed after Delegations, plus two calls added to `features/settings/api.ts`.

The request didn't list every place a claim gets created, so I applied the holiday rule to all four places that fix a due-by:
- adding a claim
- splitting a claim
- pasting claims
- quick-add's check for a closed period

Re-dating a claim isn't covered, because it already keeps the existing due-by.

The refusals reuse the existing settings error type rather than a new holiday one, so they come back through the same handler as an invalid setting.
